contexts.text: The flying thing came down upon the bodies () = the evils and derivative falsities which wanted to destroy. The flying thing = falsity. A flying thing in the Word = truth, and also in the opposite sense falsity.
The transformation of caterpillars into flying things.
Birds which fly high... = rational things.

The fifth degree of their vastation is that they were in falsities from these evils, by which all truth was destroyed; these are signified by the baneful flying thing (). ( = the falsities of malevolence AC 7441-7465.)

The particular kind of falsities which are here signified by the baneful flying thing is (falsities in the extremes of the natural mind, thus in the Sensuous). The same are signified by the flies of Egypt ()... These falsities are compared to such an insect because the things which are there are just like flying things in the air, which obscure interior things, and also inflict injury upon them; for they are for the most part imaginary things, and are fallacies, the reasonings from which are like things based on the air. The baneful flying thing of this kind is mentioned only in  and .

All flying things in the Word = intellectual things, and therefore truths, and in the opposite sense falsities. References. But flying things of the lowest sort, which are insects, = truths and in the opposite sense falsities which are more ignoble and obscure, such as are those which are proper to the Sensuous...
A flying thing = what is spiritual or that which is of faith.
Flying animals and also winged insects = such things as are of thoughts in both senses, thus truths or falsities.

In the other life falsities from evil... are presented to view as a filthy swarm of insects and of unclean flying things, terrible to look upon according to the species of the evil from which they are. Illustrated.
To fly upon the shoulder of the Philistines () = to receive and take into possession the interior truths of faith. (Compare AE 433:7.)
They fly in the air as in their Heaven.
All the birds of the air know their food... how to build nests, etc. DLW 353.
Flying things according to their species correspond to the intellectual things of both the natural and the spiritual mind.
From a perception of their stench they fly to cadaverous and stercoraceous things.
The soul (supposed to be) something flying in the ether.

The idea (men have) of love and wisdom is as of something flying and floating in the... ether... not being aware that love and wisdom are the subject itself, and that what is perceived outside of it as flying and floating, is only the appearance of the state of the subject in itself.
(Thus) sight, hearing, etc., are not any volatile thing...
Thought, perceptions, and affections... are not volatile entities...
Nor can they think about life, except as a volatile thing...
Noxious flies fill the atmosphere...
The less perfect animals are birds.
Profaners... appear to themselves to fly on high...
See Eagle. SE 2229. AE 410:5.
To fly in the midst of heaven and say () = to perceive and understand; and when said of the Lord, to look out for and provide; here, to instruct and foretell.
To fly = to perceive and instruct.
That she might fly into the wilderness, into her place () = protection while the New Church is as yet among a few... To fly = to clearly see, and to look about.
To fly in the midst of heaven () = to look down, to clearly see, and to look out for; here, what is new from the Lord out of Heaven for the Church.

Saying to all the birds that fly in the midst of heaven () = all who are in the spiritual affection of truth, and who therefore think of Heaven... To fly in the midst of heaven = to clearly see, to attend, and to think.
I once saw an Angel flying...
There appeared one from Heaven as it were flying, having two wings at his feet and two at his temples.
In their cavern they fly about like spectres; for they are then in phantasy, and phantasy appears to fly. After their flight they rest.

Love and wisdom without use are only volatile things of reason, and also fly away unless they betake themselves to use. The first two separated from the third are like birds which fly over a great ocean, until, wearied with their flight, they fall down and sink.
As his delight is in Hell he flies down.
Dragons are flying serpents.
The Spirit flew out thence above the head.
Some flew out from that Hell.
There were a great number of Souls flying about there, who... had been vastated...

Profaners... become like spectres, and appear to themselves to fly about in the air... A female profaner has been seen so to fly, and she then has nothing of thought, for she is in infernal phantasy, which is the source of the appearance.
Acute reasoners... appear flying in ashes... DMin 4723:end.
To fly = presence, also view round about; and, when predicated of the Divine, omnipresence.

To fly, in the Word, = circumspection and presence, because when a bird is flying on high it sees clearly on every side, and thus is present everywhere by ifs sight. But when to fly is predicated of Jehovah, it = omnipresence, because omnipresence is infinite circumspection and presence. Illustrated. AE 283:5.
To fly as a cloud, and as the doves to their windows () = the inquiring into and the searching out of truth from the sense of the letter of the Word.

The inquiring into truth, and circumspection as to where to turn, is signified by, Who shall give me a wing as of a dove? I will fly away where I may dwell (). To fly away where I may dwell = through this to rescue the life from damnation.
To fly away like a bird () = the deprivation of Divine truth.
To fly towards heaven () = the circumspection which is of intelligence in Divine things.

The reason to fly, when predicated of men, = circumspection and at the same time presence, is that the sight is present with the object which it sees... Hence it is that to fly is said of the understanding and of its intelligence...
Hence profaners... appear to themselves to fly hither and thither without any thought.

There appear in the Spiritual World flying things of various kinds, but they are appearances from the ideas of the thoughts of Spirits; and the baneful flying things among them are of such a kind as flies and bees.
To fly () = to enlighten and give understanding.

The reason to fly, when predicated of the Lord, = to enlighten, is that to fly is predicated of the understanding and of the extension of its sight round about; and therefore, when predicated of the Lord, to fly = the enlightenment of the understanding. To fly, when predicated of the Lord, = omnipresence, and therefore it also = enlightenment; for wherever the Lord is present there is enlightenment. Illustrated.
The birds of heaven which devoured the seed () = falsities...
To fly away () = to be dissipated. To fly away is mentioned because a bird is mentioned.
They seem to themselves to fly in the air, like dragons.
Avolatio occurs.
In a higher degree are the birds of the air.
